cells.tense: A start is here with a shape on it, and you are close to it with the pen still moving in the open.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: The beginning under your hands is quietly asking for one concrete piece of help, done in a single sitting, finished, no invoice, no thanks needed. Give it, then leave the rest alone.
cells.core:
Something at the start is holding its shape, and you are the one who put shape on it. The people in it with you can feel it too — the direction is clear, and no one has to be talked into it. The good hour is when what you are and what you are doing are the same thing, and this is one of those.

After that, protect the seed. One plain, complete act of help is what the beginning needs: one concrete thing, done in one sitting, no invoice, no thanks required. Give it, then leave the rest alone. Give it without conditions and it stays a real gift. That is the whole act — support with nothing pretending.
cells.sheetLine: The start is holding its shape while you hold it.
cells.verb: Starting the thing in its first form and giving it a shape someone else can hold.
cells.place: The room where what you already are is becoming visible and nothing is being added to make it true.

cells.tense: You will have to know how the whole thing lands before it is anywhere near landed.
cells.act: know the feeling fully before you move on
cells.ask: About the start you are carrying: sit down once and let yourself know what you actually feel about it — all of it, unedited — before you decide anything. Nothing to fix. Just know it fully first.
cells.core:
The start has barely begun and you are already standing at its ending. Something feels unfinished, so you reach for the next thing to settle it — another plan, another push, another version. Meanwhile the start is still a start, and the ones near it are still meeting that start, not the one you are bracing for. From the far side it reads as fixing what nobody asked to have fixed.

So take one sitting, one page, and let yourself know what you actually feel about the beginning under your hands — the whole of it, every shade, unedited. Then decide if you want to. That is where the real knowing waits, and it is the only thing that makes what comes next yours instead of from the shoulder. Nothing to prove, either. Just know it, and then you can move on.

cells.tense: You had the beginning of something in your hands once and you are still standing at the door after it.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: The start you have not picked back up: lay it all out once — what it is, what is still unresolved, what you are avoiding — and look until nothing is left unseen. Then that is done, and the thing can be, too.
cells.core:
A start came and its shape was clear, and you put it down. Not out of failure — it just went quiet. Since then the door you were standing at has closed, but you are still at it, and the energy is going into standing there. What is in your hands now is smaller than what you actually carry. The beginning is yours and it is still unstarted.

So make one full look. Gather the whole of the old start onto one page or table — what it was, what is still tangled in it, what you keep not looking at — and look until there is nothing left unseen. No verdict, no restart required. When nothing is hidden, this ends, and the thing can end with it. Then, and only then, note the piece of it that still wants to be done.

cells.tense: The shaping is in your hands now, and your own account says it happened on its own.
cells.act: look at the whole of it until nothing is left to see
cells.ask: The thing quietly taking form through you: lay all of it out at once, the way you would spread papers across a table — what you have been doing, and what it adds up to — until you have seen it without adding or taking away.
cells.core:
Somewhere in this beginning, the shaping is yours. The order is being kept, the words are being placed, the timing is being held — and the account you carry says it just came together, nothing much to notice. The start is being written. You, asked, would say it wrote itself.

Catch it once. At whatever moment you are quietly doing the shaping, stop long enough to see what you are actually doing — and then keep going. Nothing has to be announced. Seeing the whole of it for one second is enough to put your name back on it, and the work is the same either way; it just stops belonging to a stranger.
cells.sheetLine: The plan is being written by your hand. You say it wrote itself.
cells.verb: Starting the thing in its first form and giving it a shape someone else can hold.
cells.place: The room where what you already are is becoming visible and nothing is being added to make it true.
